extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reporters on writing game stories and other sporting news items (football, basketball, track, golf, tennis, boxing, auto racing, billiards), including what facts to collect, how to structure accounts, and stylistic/ethical cautions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Center the reader's interest on the hero
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting a game (example: the Oliphant-centered football account), center the reader's interest upon the football hero — a stroke which gives the article almost a short story unity of impression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with or frequently return to the key performer to create unity of impression; avoid abrupt or rough shifts between crowd/game and hero (criticized example: 'We are as loyal a Democrat as anybody else, but NO,'). Use the hero-focus to make the article read like a coherent narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Getting players' names (use numbers and position mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting a football game, one can best follow and take notes on the plays by knowing the players by number; on smaller teams use numbering positions according to the regulation lineup and fill in names afterward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number positions (example layout provided) and take shorthand play notes like '4 around s 10 yds.' or '2 through 7-8 to 20-yd. line.' Fill in the players' names after each half. This overcomes missing jersey numerals on small elevens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Football play-by-play reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the game sequentially: kickoff, key runs, line plays, punts, returns, drives, defensive stands, scoring plays, and the score progression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include times (e.g., 'It was 2:18 when...'), field position (yards), specifics of key plays (who ran, who punted, blocked, fumbled, recovered), and scoring details (touchdown drive description, goal after touchdown). Use vivid but accurate action detail; examples in the text show detailed play sequences and drives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basketball reporting: quarter-by-quarter scoring and line-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Because basketball scores change rapidly, detailed accounts customarily give the exact score of each team at the end of every quarter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with a terse summary, provide a narrative of the game's flow (e.g., key runs, protest handling), supply the line-up and individual scoring table (field goals, free goals, totals), list game officials and times of halves (example: halves, 15 minutes each). To be accurate, reporters should sit next to the scorer or between students/friends of players to get names instantly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track meet reporting: use announced results and highlight records
rubrics_metrics.description: Track meets are easier to report since events run slowly and results are announced to the grandstand; summarize feature events and record performances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report winning teams/individuals, times/distances, any records set, and narrative highlights (close finishes, anchor performances). Include summaries and point scoring (e.g., three-lap relay finish and times) as shown in example summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Golf reporting: lead with full summary then hole-by-hole details
rubrics_metrics.description: Start with a substantial summary (half-dozen paragraphs if needed) describing results, character of playing, weather, links condition, and competitors; follow with a hole-by-hole detailed story including length, par, and the relative standing on each hole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide numerical summaries every nine holes and a score-by-holes table. Include context (e.g., prior meetings between players), and describe swings in the match and turning points. Examples show hole-by-hole annotations (yardage, par, what happened) and cumulative scorecards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tennis reporting: include set summaries from the scorer
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclude tennis match stories with a summary by sets (likely obtained from the scorer) and include narrative of pivotal rallies and strokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe styles of play, momentum shifts, and statistical details (points, games, aces, faults, nets, outs) where helpful. Use scorer-provided set-by-set totals and relevant stats to support narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boxing reporting: two-part structure and required facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Boxing reports should combine the methods of football (narrative) and golf (round-by-round detail). The first section is a full general account; the second is a detailed running story by rounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the general account include fighters' weights/heights/reach, methods of attack and defense, crowd description, receipts, exact start and end times, and any injuries (e.g., broken hand). Then give round-by-round play describing clinches, landed blows, defensive tactics, and critical moments. Examples show detailed rounds plus financial and attendance figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical caution: present the wholesome side of boxing
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid writing about boxing in a way that appeals to the barbaric nature of readers or revels in gore; emphasize skill, dexterity, and generalship rather than blood and brutality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose wholesome details that preserve the sport's legitimacy; avoid lurid, bloodthirsty depictions (criticized 'Spanish bull-ring' style). The reporter's point of view determines whether the account is wholesome or unwholesome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automobile race reporting: results table plus lap-by-lap narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a results table showing driver, time, and average, and complement it with a lap-by-lap narrative noting lead changes, mechanical troubles, pit stops, start times, and crowd reaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report record-breaking averages and specific incidents (e.g., tire trouble, stops and durations). Include trial lap/start procedures and key chronological developments by lap as illustrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Billiards reporting: record individual runs and averages
rubrics_metrics.description: In billiards coverage note each player's runs, the high run, and the player's average; present inning-by-inning or run-by-run scoring if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give totals and averages (examples list series of runs and compute averages like 'Average, 19 6-26'), and highlight notable high runs and turning points in the match.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining information and press logistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters are provided press tickets and seats (press-box); press-boxes usually have telegraph and telephone wires, sometimes private office wires. If immediate reporting is required and wires are absent, arrange messengers and structure notes for rapid dispatch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure at least two messengers if wires are unavailable to take bulletins quickly; take notes so that bulletins can be sent within seconds after the event. Know location/phone/telegraph facilities at the venue and use the scorer's data when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal opinion and hybrid story types
rubrics_metrics.description: Sporting stories (previews, post-game features, and general sports pieces) may be hybrids of news and editorial, presenting facts while also interpreting and influencing opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware when a piece moves from pure reporting to advocacy or prediction (example: 'Michigan has a chance' mixes lineup reporting with an editorial stance). If offering opinion, the writer should recognize the hybrid nature and choose wording appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include line-ups, box scores, officials and timing details
rubrics_metrics.description: For many sports include formal line-ups, scoring tables (field goals, free goals, totals; hole-by-hole or set-by-set cards), referee/official names, and timing (length of halves, exact start/end times).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide tabulated totals and team/player line-ups as exemplified (basketball lineup table, golf score-by-holes, tennis set scores, referee credit). These items aid reader understanding and enable verification.
